best_for: Musicians and sound designers on Windows, Mac or Linux who want a free, deep synthesizer to load in their DAW or play on its own, including on older machines.

points.title: Free and GPL-3.0
points.text: Surge XT is open source under GPL-3.0, developed on GitHub by the Surge Synth Team, which says everything it makes is free. It is a hybrid subtractive synth with 12 oscillator types, a filter block, a modulation engine and 27 effects.

points.title: Plugin formats depend on the system
points.text: Windows hosts get VST3 and CLAP, Mac hosts get VST3, AU and CLAP, and Linux hosts get VST3, CLAP and LV2. A standalone app is included on all three, so you can play it without a DAW.

points.title: Runs on old hardware
points.text: The minimum is Windows 7 on a CPU with SSE2, or macOS 10.11 on an Intel Mac, while Apple silicon Macs need only an Apple silicon version of macOS. The team asks for at least 4 GB of RAM on every system.

points.title: Windows installers in this listing
points.text: Each release here has 64-bit and 32-bit Inno Setup installers, and the Windows listing keeps 7 versions, from 1.1.2 to 1.3.4. The release page also offers plugin-only zips and a portable 64-bit zip, which are not listed here.

points.title: The stable release dates from 2024
points.text: Version 1.3.4 came out on 11 August 2024. Newer work ships as nightly builds made from every commit, which the team warns can have bugs and loud glitches, so it suggests a limiter. Patches saved in a nightly may not load the same way in later versions.

points.title: Mac and Linux keep only the current build
points.text: The Mac download is a universal DMG for Intel and Apple silicon. Linux comes here as the Flathub package for x64 and Arm64, the standalone app, which Flathub does not mark as verified. The project's own .deb, .rpm and tar.gz files are not listed. Both keep only version 1.3.4.
